words.meaning: to throw away or get rid of something that is no longer useful
words.scene: When cleaning a training set, you often discard samples with missing labels.
words.example: The preprocessing script will discard any image that fails the quality check.

words.meaning: to cause something to start or happen
words.scene: In an agent system, a user message can trigger a chain of tool calls.
words.example: A sudden drop in accuracy may trigger an automatic rollback of the deployed model.

words.meaning: to find the way through a place or system; to steer a course
words.scene: Autonomous drones must navigate crowded airspace without human control.
words.example: The robot uses a depth camera to navigate around obstacles in real time.

words.meaning: to adjust an instrument or model so its measurements are accurate
words.scene: Before collecting data, engineers calibrate every camera and lidar unit.
words.example: We calibrate the confidence scores so the model does not appear overconfident.

words.meaning: to combine separate parts into a coherent whole; to produce artificially
words.scene: In a literature review, you synthesize results from many papers into one argument.
words.example: The system can synthesize realistic speech from a short text prompt.

words.meaning: the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; unclearness
words.scene: Natural language prompts often contain ambiguity that the model must resolve.
words.example: The paper discusses how to handle ambiguity in user instructions for AI agents.

words.meaning: to disturb or change something slightly, often to test stability
words.scene: Adversarial attacks perturb images so that classifiers make wrong predictions.
words.example: Researchers perturb the parameters slightly to see whether performance remains stable.

words.meaning: to control and use the power of something for a purpose
words.collocation: harness the power of large models
words.scene: Startups try to harness large language models to automate customer support.
words.example: The team harnessed GPU clusters to train the model in only three days.

words.meaning: to make something worse in quality or performance
words.scene: Too much noise in the data can degrade the accuracy of a model.
words.example: Long conversations may degrade an agent's ability to track earlier instructions.

words.meaning: to examine something very carefully and critically
words.scene: Reviewers scrutinize the experimental setup before accepting a paper.
words.example: We should scrutinize the baseline numbers to make sure the comparison is fair.
